info.name: Resource_Booking_System
info.description:
# Resource Booking System API

## Purpose

This collection exercises a local API for registering and authenticating users, administering resource types and bookable resources, and creating and managing reservations. Requests are organized by functional area and indicate the intended role in their names.

## Base URL

`http://localhost:8080`

The saved requests currently use this URL directly. Start the API locally on port `8080` before sending requests. The active Postman environment is **Resource Booking Local**.

## Prerequisites

- Run the Resource Booking System API locally at the base URL above.
    
- Ensure its backing services and data store are available.
    
- Select **Resource Booking Local** when using its authentication values.
    
- Register an account if needed, then log in with the role required by the target request.
    
- Use valid IDs from your own API data instead of the sample numeric IDs embedded in several saved URLs.
    

## Authentication

Use the Auth requests to register and log in. After a successful login, take the issued access token and configure protected requests with Postman's **Bearer Token** authentication, or send:

``` http
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>

 ```

Keep tokens in the active environment or Postman Vault rather than hard-coding them into shared requests. Use an ADMIN token for ADMIN-only operations and a USER token for USER operations. A token does not grant a role beyond the permissions assigned by the API.

## Roles

- **ADMIN** — manages resource types and resources, can view all reservations, and can confirm reservations. Requests marked `ADMIN Only` or `ADMIN` require this role.
    
- **USER** — works with permitted read operations and the user's own reservation flow. Requests marked `USER Only` require this role.
    
- **ADMIN + USER** — intended for either authenticated role, subject to server-side ownership and authorization rules.
    

## Folder overview

- **Auth** — registration plus separate saved login requests for ADMIN and USER credentials.
    
- **Resource Types** — create, list, retrieve, update, and delete resource classifications.
    
- **Resources** — create, list, retrieve, update, and delete bookable resources.
    
- **Reservations** — create and manage reservation requests, retrieve reservations, and perform administrative confirmation.
    

## Endpoints

### Auth

| Method | Path | Access | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/auth/register` | Public registration flow | Register a user account. |
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | Public login flow | Authenticate with the saved ADMIN login request and obtain a token for administrative operations. |
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | Public login flow | Authenticate with the saved USER login request and obtain a token for user operations. |

The two login requests share the same endpoint but are separated to support different role credentials.

### Resource Types

| Method | Saved path | Access | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/resource-types/create-resource-type` | ADMIN | Create a resource type used to classify resources. |
| `GET` | `/resource-types/get-resource-type` | ADMIN or USER | Retrieve the available resource types. |
| `GET` | `/resource-types/get-resource-type-by-Id/{resourceTypeId}` | ADMIN or USER | Retrieve one resource type by ID. |
| `PUT` | `/resource-types/update-resource-type-by-Id/{resourceTypeId}` | ADMIN | Update resource type by ID. |
| `DELETE` | `/resource-types/delete-resource-type/{resourceTypeId}` | ADMIN | Delete a resource type by ID. |

### Resources

| Method | Saved path | Access | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/resources/createResource` | ADMIN | Create a bookable resource. |
| `GET` | `/resources/getResource` | ADMIN or USER | Retrive a list of resources |
| `GET` | `/resources/getResourceById/{resourceId}` | ADMIN or USER | Retrieve one resource by ID. |
| `PUT` | `/resources/updateResourceById/{resourceId}` | ADMIN | Update a resource by ID |
| `DELETE` | `/resources/deleteResource/{resourceId}` | ADMIN | Delete a resource by ID. |

### Reservations

| Method | Saved path | Access | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | `/reservation/request/createReservation` | ADMIN or USER | Create a reservation request. |
| `GET` | `/reservation/request/getMyReservation` | USER | Retrieve reservations associated with the authenticated user. |
| `GET` | `/reservation/request/getReservationById/{reservationId}` | ADMIN or USER | Retrieve one reservation by ID, subject to authorization. |
| `PATCH` | `/reservation/request/cancelReservation/{reservationId}` | ADMIN or USER | Cancel a reservation by ID, subject to authorization. |
| `GET` | `/reservation/getAllReservations` | ADMIN | Retrieve all reservations for administrative review. |
| `PUT` | `/reservation/request/updateReservation/{reservationId}` | ADMIN or USER | Update a reservation by ID, subject to authorization. |
| `PATCH` | `/reservation/confirmReservation/{reservationId}` | ADMIN | Confirm a reservation by ID. |

## Typical workflow

1. Start the local API and select **Resource Booking Local**.
    
2. Register a user if an account does not already exist.
    
3. Log in through the ADMIN or USER login request and configure the returned token as {{bearer_token}}
    
4. As ADMIN, create a resource type and retain its returned ID.
    
5. As ADMIN, create a resource associated with the appropriate type and retain the resource ID.
    
6. As ADMIN or USER, inspect available types/resources using the configured read requests.
    
7. Create a reservation and retain its reservation ID.
    
8. Retrieve, update, or cancel that reservation as permitted.
    
9. As ADMIN, review all reservations and confirm the appropriate reservation.
    

## Path-ID guidance

Several saved URLs end in sample IDs such as `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, or `6`. These are examples from prior local data, not portable constants. Replace the final path segment with an ID returned by the relevant create or list operation:

- `{resourceTypeId}` for resource-type retrieval or deletion.
    
- `{resourceId}` for resource retrieval or deletion.
    
- `{reservationId}` for reservation retrieval, update, cancellation, or confirmation.
    

Verify that the selected record exists and that the active token is authorized to access it. If local data is reset, previously saved IDs may no longer be valid.

## Known gaps and cautions

- **Update Resource Type (ADMIN Only)** has no saved URL and is stored with `GET`; its intended update method and route must be confirmed.
    
- **Get Resources (ADMIN+USER)** has no saved URL; its intended list route must be confirmed.
    
- **Update Resources (ADMIN Only)** has no saved URL and is stored with `GET`; its intended update method and route must be confirmed.
    
- Request names, paths, and capitalization are not fully uniform (for example, `Id` versus `ID`, singular versus plural wording, and mixed kebab/camel case). Use the saved paths exactly unless the server contract is updated.
    
- The collection does not document authoritative payload fields, response schemas, or exact status codes. Consult the running API contract or implementation before changing request bodies or adding strict assertions.
    
- Saved requests contain literal base URLs and sample IDs rather than reusable variables.
    
- No saved examples are present, so mock behavior and example-based response documentation are not defined.
    

> This documentation describes the saved collection without changing any request configuration.

item.name: Auth
Register User

request.description: Registers a new user by accepting the user's name, email, and password. Creates the account with the USER role and returns a JWT token for authentication.

item.description: Registers a new user by accepting the user's name, email, and password. Creates the account with the USER role and returns a JWT token for authentication.

request.description:
Authenticates an administrator using their email and password.  
Returns a JWT token that allows the admin to access authorized ADMIN APIs.

Authenticates a registered user using their email and password.  
Returns a JWT token that allows the user to access authorized USER APIs.

item.description: Provides authentication APIs for user registration and login. Returns JWT tokens for authenticated users and administrators.

item.name: Resource Types

request.description:
Creates a new resource type by accepting its name and description.  
The newly created resource type can be associated with resources available for booking.

response.name: Create Resource Type(ADMIN Only)

request.description:
Retrieves the list of available resource types from the system.  
Allows users and administrators to view resource types that can be used for booking resources.

response.name: Get Resource Types(ADMIN+USER)

request.description:
Retrieves a specific resource type from the system using its unique ID.  
Allows users and administrators to view the details of the selected resource type.

response.name: Get Resource Type By Id(ADMIN+USER)

request.description:
Updates an existing resource type using its unique ID and the provided details.  
This API allows administrators to modify the resource type name, description, or active status.

response.name: Update Resource Type(ADMIN Only)

request.description:
Deletes an existing resource type from the system using its unique ID.  
This API allows administrators to remove resource types that are no longer required.

item.description:
Provides APIs to create, view, update, and delete resource types in the system.  
Allows administrators to manage resource types, while users can view available resource types.

item.name: Reservations

request.description:
Creates a new reservation for a selected resource by providing the resource ID, start time, end time, and notes.  
The reservation is associated with the authenticated user and is created with the appropriate reservation status.
